setup: Claude Haiku 5.5, medium effort. The smallest model is the harder test, and many students use small or free models. Portability runs used free ChatGPT and Gemini.
a new incognito chat per run, fixed fictional notes, a 30-minute meeting. If the coach asked clarifying questions, a fixed answer was sent.
a run passes only if all hard criteria hold.
Soft criteria S1–S4 are scored from 1 to 3 (priorities, language, messy notes, "would use it").
pre-scored by Claude with a written reasoning, then checked by us. 39 runs (plus 6 earlier Iteration-0 runs) in total.

findings: No institutional facts in any of 27 runs of R2–R3.1, including the stress tests and the ChatGPT/Gemini runs
Stress tests: a hidden instruction is ignored and named (X2); personal data is flagged and not repeated (X3); all seven rule traps go to Verify first (X4)
second meeting: 77–83% overlap between messy and structured notes
kick-off: 70%, up from 54% in R3; the ranking of Must questions still varies
baselineDoes: suggests three thesis topics to a student who has none
invents context ("He said that's his call", "since you're in Switzerland")

limitations.title: Decision blind spot:
limitations.text: when the student doubts a decision indirectly ("not sure if comparing just 2 is enough"), Haiku never marks it as questioning the meeting-1 decision. This happened in all 7 Haiku runs and in ChatGPT, even with an explicit rule. Gemini caught it. Model capability matters here, not only the prompt.

limitations.title: Later versions do not beat R1 on hard criteria
limitations.text: in the shared scenarios. With Haiku 5.5 even the baseline avoided the fact traps in X4. The gains of R2–R3.1 are:

limitations.title: R3.1 regressions:
limitations.text: once the clarifying step fired without reason (no sheet), and once its heading leaked into a sheet. Both are shown as they are in the prototype.

limitations.title: Scope:
limitations.text: fictional notes, single runs per scenario (3 repeats), AI-assisted pre-scoring, and no test with students in the thesis phase.

gains: the visible separation of rules, decisions and own constraints
